predecessor: PR29 implementation and partial meta-materialization engineering tests; no previous residency ownership experiment is claimed.
question: Does the dictionary cache budget also bound persistent CPU weight storage owned by a module across repeated materialize_module calls?
hypothesis: The union of live CPU storage reachable from the module and cache remains no larger than the declared one-shard serialized-byte budget at every completed request.
scope: Fresh artificial CPU systems mechanism falsification only. The explicit cache-dictionary contract and a stronger whole-module residency interpretation are separate.

fixture.weight_rule: W_i=(i+1)*I_128, named layer{i}.weight; no gradients or optimization

budget_rule: B=max(actual serialized file sizes); require every shard <=100000 bytes, 65536 <= B < 131072, and 2*min(file sizes)>B. Each plan must select exactly the requested single shard.
control: Each arm runs in a separate fresh process with the same fixture bytes, cache budget, six plans, six selected-layer forwards, and exactly six disk loads. The control releases the preceding module and creates a fresh meta module before the next materialization; the PR29 loader remains unmodified.
primary_metric: For each step after forward temporaries are deleted and gc.collect returns, sum unique untyped CPU storage nbytes reachable from current model parameters/buffers or store._cache tensors. Deduplicate by (data_ptr,nbytes). This is a lower bound on live process storage, not RSS.
secondary_metrics: weak-reference liveness of previous parameter/tensor owners
exact output equality and SHA256 of little-endian float32 values
disk loads and resident shard IDs
child maximum RSS and host/cgroup memory and swap observations
falsifier: Any persistent-module primary metric > B while all selected outputs are exact and all cache/plan/fixture controls pass, with the recreated-module control remaining <=B.

decision_rules.RESIDENCY_INTERPRETATION_FALSIFIED: All 12 requests are valid, control <= B at all steps, persistent > B at one or more steps. This rejects the whole-module interpretation, not the narrower serialized dictionary-cache limit.
decision_rules.NOT_FALSIFIED_IN_BOUND: Both arms valid and both remain <=B. This finite trace cannot establish a global residency or process-memory guarantee.
decision_rules.INCONCLUSIVE: Execution completes but the recreated-module control also exceeds B, so the ownership contrast does not isolate the interpretation.
decision_rules.INVALID: Hash, runtime, fixture, plan, output, disk-load matching, instrumentation, or execution contract fails; preserve partial evidence and do not interpret the primary hypothesis.
decision_rules.BLOCKED: The shared workload lock, Linux host/cgroup >=2 GiB effective available memory, <=90% swap rule, or fixed wall budget prevents execution.

stopping_rule: Execute the single predeclared three-process matrix once; stop after both six-step arms or the first contract/resource/time failure. No seed, trace, dimension, threshold, baseline, or mechanism changes after viewing outcomes. A necessary harness repair requires a new version and retains this attempt.
exclusions: No consumed v2/v3/v4/v5 or EditCLEVR samples/checkpoints
No Hermes benchmark, promotion, training, external data, network, GPU, paid job, remote mutation, or Worldcastr
No LLM quality, throughput, prefetch usefulness, total peak RAM, Mac/16 GB support, or novelty conclusion
No allocator-release conclusion from weakref expiration or RSS
resource_policy_amendment: Before first execution, adopt the parent-reviewed conservative file-cache-credit estimate; raw headroom remains separately recorded and the 2 GiB floor is unchanged. No hypothesis outcomes informed this amendment.
cgroup_cache_credit: min(used, max(0, min(inactive_file,file)-shmem-file_mapped-file_dirty-file_writeback)); require all nonnegative counters, else zero credit; v1 uses corresponding total_* counters.
